triage_candidates.statement: tc11 (FLOAT, contradicting evidence -- not decided by me). A THIRD stale-claim family exists that no sweep on this lane has ever hunted, and it is live and UNFENCED. I MEASURED that these are false as shipped rather than inferring it: driving a spine whose origin.worktree is '/totally/elsewhere' from a foreign cwd, both claim and start return rc=0. Sharper still, tests/test_explorer_templates.py cites the 2026-08-15 worktree-identity ruling as LIVE authority for that behaviour, while checklist_engine's module header says this change SUPERSEDES that ruling -- so one of the six preserved supersession citations sits inside a passage asserting the superseded behaviour as current. Why I do NOT block on it: it is outside both families the gate defined, outside the gate's Allowed Scope (the implementer could not have repaired it without exceeding scope, and its stop condition would have forced a stop that this gate cannot itself resolve), and it is the same class as the already-reported tc-A residue. Better still, the test could snapshot only paths outside the current crew's work-id subtree.

tc12 (fourth data point, re-raising the implementer's tc-B and my predecessor's tc-A). The prose block still has NO repo-level guard. Three crews have now hand-written a clause checker under .agent-work/ -- check_three_copies.py, then check_claims_repaired.py -- each covering a different subset of the copies, and the gap between subsets is where each round's defect lived. Every one of them dies with the crew that wrote it. This round's check_claims_repaired.py is the best of them (six segments, red at base and green on the tree) and it will die too. Roughly 120 lines -- the segment extractor plus the clause table -- promoted into tests/ would make the guard outlive the crew and would have caught B1 at implement time.
